reason: The text contains only four named characters: Moses (מֹשֶׁה), Aaron (אַהֲרֹן), Pharaoh (פַּרְעֹה), and God (יְהוָה). All of these function as leaders or supreme authority within the narrative. Moses and Aaron are leaders of the Israelites who mediate between God and the people, Pharaoh is the political ruler of Egypt, and God is the ultimate authority commanding all actions. All other individuals mentioned in the passage—taskmasters (נֹגְשִׂים), officers (שֹׁטְרִים), magicians (חַרְטֻמִּים), servants, and the general population—remain unnamed and collectively referenced.
